holidays.name: National Dessert Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to indulging your sweet tooth with cake, pie, cookies, ice cream, or whatever sugary masterpiece calls to you. Dinner is optional; dessert first is encouraged.
holidays.origin: National Dessert Day is an unofficial food holiday that has been celebrated in the United States for years, popularized by food bloggers and restaurants. Its exact founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dessert' comes from the French 'desservir,' meaning 'to clear the table,' so originally dessert marked the moment the table was cleared of the main meal.

holidays.name: Boss's Day
holidays.description: A day when employees are encouraged to thank their bosses with cards, small gifts, or kind words. It is celebrated with varying levels of sincerity and cake in break rooms.
holidays.origin: Patricia Bays Haroski registered the holiday with Illinois in 1958 to honor her father, who was her boss at State Farm Insurance. The date was chosen as his birthday, and in 1962 the governor of Illinois officially proclaimed it.
holidays.funFact: Haroski was working as a secretary at State Farm when she created the day. The holiday is observed on October 16 or the nearest weekday in many places.

holidays.name: World Food Day
holidays.description: A global observance focused on fighting hunger and promoting food security. Events include community meals, educational programs, and campaigns for sustainable agriculture.
holidays.origin: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations was founded on October 16, 1945. Member countries established World Food Day in 1979 to mark the anniversary and promote action against hunger.
holidays.funFact: World Food Day is observed in more than 150 countries, making it one of the most widely celebrated UN days of the year.

holidays.name: Global Cat Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate cats of every size, fluffiness, and attitude. It encourages people to keep cats safe, support shelters, and spoil their feline overlords with extra treats.
holidays.origin: Global Cat Day was started in 2013 by Alley Cat Allies, a US advocacy group, to promote cat welfare and responsible care for both pet and community cats.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep 12 to 16 hours a day, which means a cat who is celebrating Global Cat Day will probably sleep through most of it.

holidays.name: Dictionary Day
holidays.description: A day for word nerds to celebrate dictionaries, vocabulary, and the joy of looking up a word and getting lost in twelve others on the way. Try learning a new word and using it in conversation.
holidays.origin: Dictionary Day honors the birthday of Noah Webster, born October 16, 1758. He was the lexicographer behind the first American dictionary and the author of 'An American Dictionary of the English Language.'
holidays.funFact: Noah Webster's 1828 dictionary contained about 70,000 words and is credited with spelling reforms like 'color' instead of 'colour' and 'center' instead of 'centre.'
